<!-- pr-reviewer: 882ceb6f22f4036012e8a821f9c7d447b6bd5c1e -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the cut).

**What looks good**
- Re-index math (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`, `Body::carry`): the image lattice origin is the min corner of the transformed lattice bbox, with the same cell and the full `nx*cell` x `ny*cell` extent. So every column centre lands on a cell centre (k+0.5) of the image grid, whatever the translation, odd/even cell counts or partial last cell. No half-cell offset arises and nothing is interpolated. `LatticeTurn::from_matrix` accepts only signed permutations with Z on +-Z and det=+1; mirrors, side-on and non-quarter turns are refused by name (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` plus the mirror text). A lattice that cannot hold a column returns Err instead of guessing.
- Two-sided roles: flip gives `top' = tz - floor`, `floor' = tz - top`. Infinities map correctly (-inf to +inf). Double flip returns home, and `floor_judged` stays set. The bottom verdict mirrors Z and re-runs `deviate`, so `dev = part_bottom - floor`: floor above the part bottom reads as gouge, below as rest. A column cut through stays cut through after a flip. The pre-flip gouge shows up as a floor-side gouge (pinned by `a_gouge_cut_before_the_flip_is_still_judged_after_it`). A never-flipped body returns the plain `deviate` result, so single-setup verdicts are untouched (golden_cl, stock_sim_document green).
- Transform direction agrees with `parts_facets_in` (`T = A_to * A_from^-1`, `p_to = T p_from`). Refusals are named with both setups on the program-sim path, so the post gate shows "not judged". Lathe, rotary and posed programs are refused before the walk. No unwrap/expect/panic in the new code; index math is bounds-checked. Provenance lines and the decision file are present. Files are 364 (`stock_sim.rs`) and 345 (`carry.rs`) lines. PR body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #317`.

**Local results** (trial merge with origin/main was clean; no build.rs, .github, scripts or dependency changes)
| check | result |
|---|---|
| sim: stock_carry / stock_sim / stock_columns / stock_backend_parity | 6 / 24 / 3 / 13 passed |
| app --lib | 95 passed |
| app: setup_carry 5, setup_align 9, setup_relative 8, setups 11, stock_sim_document 9, posting 17, golden_cl 23, post_not_judged 4, lathe_field_sim 6, rotary_field_parity 3 (+1 ignored) | all passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. A carried setup's own stock is ignored with no diagnostic (`stock_sim_carry.rs` `walk`, `Entry::Carry`). Reading a larger or different stock there could only under-report rest, never hide a gouge, because the body is always what the earlier setup left. A user who set a bigger stock for setup 2 gets no hint it is unused. Please make #320 surface this (the "Its own stock" label on the setup page is stale meanwhile).
2. The decision note says different machines are refused. In the sim I could only find `machine::kind_of`, which reads the active setup's machine, so the lathe/mill-turn refusal depends on which setup is active. Mixed mounts are blocked at post by `setup_mount::program_problems`, and lathe ops are refused by `refuse_unjudged`, so I see no gouge path. Reading each setup's own machine kind in `entry` would be sturdier.
3. `merge` in `Body::deviate` adds rest/gouge cell counts and volumes from both sides. A column with both a top rest and a floor gouge is counted in both aggregates, though its per-column `dev` shows the gouge. This is conservative.
4. Tests use matching footprints. A case with an odd cell count and a translation that is not a multiple of the cell would pin the alignment argument above.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
